svg.title: Dashboard read, before and after
svg.desc: Before: the qualification decision was made every time the dashboard was read, by searching through the raw stored Apollo or HeyReach reply, which the database must fetch and unpack in full for every candidate row. It cost 1,092 milliseconds and excluded none of the rows it examined. After: the decision is worked out once when the activity is written, and the read is served entirely from an index, at 91 milliseconds, without touching the stored replies at all.
svg.text: BEFORE
Decided every time the dashboard opens
search the raw stored Apollo or HeyReach reply,
once for every candidate row
Those replies are large, so the database fetches and unpacks
each one in full to answer one yes-or-no question. The planner
does not price that work, so it never surfaces as a cost.
And it excluded none of the rows it examined
AFTER
Decided once, the moment it is written
read the stored answer straight from an index,
the reply itself is never opened
The database keeps that answer current on its own, because
activity arrives by more than one path, and a path someone
forgot would quietly drop buyers out of every sales view.
The read stopped touching the stored replies
DASHBOARD READ, MEASURED IN PRODUCTION
before
after
91 ms
Same rule, same result: decided at write time instead of read time.
